skill.name: brewpage-publish
skill.description: Publish text, Markdown, JSON, files, or static sites to brewpage.app with explicit access choices and private local owner-token history.
skill.summary: Share content through brewpage.app with namespace selection, optional password protection, and verified static-site bundles.
skill.author: kochetkov-ma

security_audit.summary: All 260 static alerts match documentation, exclusion patterns, intended service endpoints, or defensive local operations. A separate high-severity multipart path injection can upload unintended local files through crafted filenames. No evidence found of prompt injection or deliberate credential exfiltration.

remediation.issue: File and supplied-ZIP paths enter curl -F syntax without escaping, allowing commas to select unintended local files.
remediation.suggestion: Copy each validated source into the private run directory under a fixed safe basename before upload. Add regression tests for comma and semicolon filenames.

semantic_findings.description: Upload paths enter curl multipart syntax without filename escaping. A crafted existing path containing commas can select additional readable local files, sending their contents outside the approved source.

content.user_title: Publish Content and Static Sites to Brewpage
content.value_statement: Sharing a document or static demo often requires separate hosting setup. This skill uploads selected content to brewpage.app and returns a shareable link.
actual_capabilities: Route text, JSON, local files, directories, and ZIP archives to the corresponding publication API.
Ask for explicit namespace and password choices before uploading content.
Build static-site ZIP bundles using extension allowlists and exclude hidden entries, dependencies, and symlinks.
Inspect archive integrity and size budgets, print a manifest, and require confirmation for flagged entries.
Stage long text across commands and support requested retention, entry-file selection, and delivery mode.
Save returned owner tokens in private local history with Git exclusion checks instead of displaying them in chat.
limitations: Requires macOS, Linux, or WSL with shell utilities and POSIX Python; sites need Node.js and archive tools.
Hosts static content through an external service with retention and upload limits; it does not build projects or run application servers.
Checks archive filenames, not embedded secrets; unlisted links remain readable by anyone holding the link unless password protected.
An audited multipart path flaw can upload unintended local files through crafted filenames; fix it before accepting untrusted paths.

use_cases.title: Share Documentation
use_cases.description: Publish a selected Markdown guide or release note and share its returned link with readers.

use_cases.title: Review Static Prototypes
use_cases.description: Upload a built static demo with its assets and a chosen entry file for stakeholder review.

use_cases.title: Distribute Temporary Reports
use_cases.description: Share an approved report file or JSON dataset with explicit visibility choices and a requested retention period.

prompt_templates.title: Publish a Short Note
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish this note to brewpage.app: [approved text]. Ask me to choose the namespace and password option before uploading.

prompt_templates.title: Share a Report File
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish [absolute report path] for three days. Show its size and MIME type, then ask for namespace and password choices.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: share an approved local file.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy a Built Static Site
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish [absolute build directory] with [entry file]. Review the archive manifest and ask before including flagged entries. Confirm visibility and password choices.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: deploy build output with assets.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect and Publish an Archive
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [absolute ZIP path], check current limits, and use [entry file] with subdomain delivery. Require explicit access choices and approval for flagged entries.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: inspect an existing site archive before publishing.

output_examples.input: Publish an approved Markdown report without password protection.
output: Published: [exact reader URL returned by brewpage.app]
Owner token saved in private project history.
Unlisted link: anyone with the link can open it.

output_examples.input: Publish a static-site archive containing a sensitive-looking filename.
output: Review the manifest and flagged filenames before deciding whether to proceed.

output_examples.input: Publish a directory without an HTML entry file.
output_examples.output: Publish failed: no HTML entry found. Build the site first and select its output directory.

best_practices: Review the selected content and manifest for secrets before publishing; use built static output rather than project sources.
Choose visibility and password protection explicitly; keep passwords in local files and owner tokens out of chat.
Resolve the multipart path flaw before using untrusted filenames, and verify the returned URL and asset paths after publication.
anti_patterns: Treating an unlisted namespace as access control or uploading personal data to public listings.
Assuming filename allowlists detect embedded credentials or make arbitrary archives safe.
Expecting the skill to build application sources, run backend services, or provide permanent hosting.

faq.question: Which content types can I publish?
faq.answer: Text, Markdown, JSON, individual files, built static directories, and prebuilt site ZIP archives are supported.

faq.question: Is an unlisted namespace private?
faq.answer: It avoids public listings, but anyone with the link can read the content unless you enable password protection.

faq.question: How does password protection work?
faq.answer: Select an existing local password file with at least four characters. The script sends its contents through a private header file.

faq.question: Where are owner tokens stored?
faq.answer: They are saved in .claude/brewpage-history.md at the project root with mode 0600 and Git exclusion checks.

faq.question: How long does a publication remain available?
faq.answer: The requested default is 15 days. Service limits and deduplication affect retention; the returned expiration is authoritative.

faq.question: Does archive inspection guarantee safe uploads?
faq.answer: No. It checks structure and filenames, not embedded secrets. The audit also identified multipart path parsing that needs remediation.
